conditions: The baseline and candidate use the same scenario prompt, fixture, sandbox profile, capability profile and deadline.
The candidate installs the target skill and appends its target-use instruction; the baseline does neither.
The measured path, workload, project gate and reported samples remain comparable.

prompt: The runnable project in evals/files/measurement-decisions exposes its real inventory HTTP endpoint and has a project-owned median latency gate but no universal performance target. Run the benchmark, gate and profiler, keep those decisions separate, find the dominant cost and make the smallest behavior-preserving optimization. Keep filtered output, ordering and the gate value unchanged. Report raw before/after samples and the ratio.
expected_output: The response measures the real HTTP path before changing code, reports the benchmark samples separately from the project gate and profiler attribution, identifies repeated all-item scanning and profile work as the dominant cause, preserves duplicate removal, report fields, ordering and the project gate constant, and reports comparable raw samples, aggregates and a negative control.
assertions: The response measures the production HTTP endpoint rather than a copied benchmark algorithm.
The response reports benchmark samples, the project gate decision and profiler attribution as separate decisions.
The response identifies repeated all-item scanning and per-item profile work as the dominant cost.
The candidate preserves duplicate removal, report fields, ordering and the unchanged gate value.
The response reports raw before/after samples, an aggregate, a negative control and the ratio.
The edited project's focused test passes.
